gloss: Exaggerated words that don't match reality.
teaser: Let's explore the art of overstatement and its implications in daily life.
script: Welcome to Chengyu Bites — your quick summary on Chinese 成语. Let's explore the art of overstatement and its implications in daily life.[break 1s] The phrase is: 言过其实, yán guò qí shí.[break 1s] 言 (yán) - speech, words[break 0.5s] 过 (guò) - too much, excessive[break 0.5s] 其 (qí) - its, that[break 0.5s] 实 (shí) - reality, truth[break 0.5s] Full idiom again: 言过其实 literally means 'words exceed reality', figuratively implying that someone is exaggerating.[break 1s] Here’s the story behind it:[break 1.5s] The phrase originates from ancient texts where scholars discussed the importance of honesty in communication. There was a warning against those who would embellish tales, leading listeners astray. This caution was essential in maintaining trust and credibility in society. Over time, it evolved into a common expression used to call out exaggeration.[break 1.5s] Examples: 他总是言过其实，让人难以相信。He always exaggerates, making it hard for people to believe him.[break 1s] 这篇文章言过其实，缺乏真实的数据。This article is exaggerated, lacking real data.[break 1s] 我们应该避免言过其实，以免失去信任。We should avoid exaggeration to prevent losing trust.[break 1s] 言过其实 means exaggerating words that don't match reality. Thanks for listening to Chengyu Bites! See you next time for another idiom.[break 1s]
